title: Garni Temple
visualBrief: Restored basalt peripteral temple with twenty-four smooth entasis columns assembled in drums, Ionic spiral capitals, an open cella doorway and barrel vault, sculpted entablature, dentils, coffered portico soffits, paired pediments, individual stone roof tiles, palmette acroteria and nine steps flanked by kneeling relief figures.

nativeAxes.front: +Z is the northern entrance and nine-step stair; signed geographic fit requires review
nativeAxes.origin: Temple axis in plan, at the bottom-stair ground datum

scaleBasis: Sahinyan’s restoration measurements define the podium, order, column axes, doorway and cella. Modern photographs establish smooth drum shafts, varied restoration stones and carved decorative zones. The broad OSM outline is not used to stretch the measured temple dimensions.

geographicProposal.evidence: Attributed cached OSM way108255791 exactQ684072, captured2026-09-27, establishes the site anchor[44.730218747,40.11234151] and long axis. The signed heading−2.886586468439rad puts native+Z toward north-northwest,14.61°west of true north, and native+X west-southwest. The university research record explicitly identifies the northern entrance facade; original front, flank and rear photographs confirm stair and cella sidedness. The mapped rectangle exceeds the measured podium and is a comparison control only. Stair projection extends toward the northern forecourt; no whole-ensemble stretch. Approximate5m/5° placement, not a survey.
geographicProposal.limitations: Complete static medium-fi exterior of the reconstructed Garni temple: measured6-by8 arrangement with24Ionic columns, entasis and bases, open cella doorway and visible vaulted chamber, high podium and nine entrance steps with paired relief cheeks, open peristyle walks and coffered ceiling, molded entablature/dentils, two triangular pediments, basalt tile roof and palmette acroteria. The original1209054triangle source recipe remains reproducible; the reviewed full master retains that detailed sculpture and corrects the podium stair recess so all nine steps stay exposed. Four whole-temple browser levels reduce roundness, drum joints, ashlar blocks, capital curls and sculpted motifs. Sculpture is a stylized interpretation, not a reproduction of each distinct ancient vine, lion, coffer or human portrait. Photograph and map registration are approximate; the broad mapped rectangle is retained as a comparison and does not rescale the measured temple. Position tolerance5m and heading5° acknowledge generalized mapping and unsurveyed stair offset. Ground0 is the bottom stair/site platform. The separate palace, bathhouse, church ruins, canyon, adjacent precinct and visitor objects are not part of this temple asset. Absolute elevation, detailed surrounding grade and physical phone/laptop timings remain unmeasured.
